angle: Interpretability of the specific architectures used on traffic: transformers/attention and GNNs
method: Semantic Scholar Graph API (search + citation expansion of ET-BERT and YaTC), arXiv API, DBLP API, WebSearch; abstracts retrieved for all entries; ET-BERT and YaTC full PDFs text-mined to verify interpretability claims
key_question_answer: No faithfulness/validation study of attention weights in ET-BERT, YaTC, or TrafficFormer exists in the retrieved literature. Verified from full text: ET-BERT's 'Interpretability' section (4.4, WWW'22) is a cipher-randomness analysis plus t-SNE of representations -- no attention attribution; YaTC's AAAI'23 paper contains no interpretability analysis at all (attention is purely architectural: packet-level/flow-level modules, ablated only for accuracy); TrafficFormer (S&P'25) claims no explainability and its repo advertises none. The NLP 'attention is not explanation' debate has not been imported into the traffic domain. Closest existing work: (a) SAM (Computer Networks 2021) reads raw self-attention weights as byte/header importance for plaintext-header traffic; (b) a 2026 neurosymbolic APT paper (arXiv 2603.00453) aggregates per-layer/head [CLS] attention over 14 flow-feature tokens and statistically validates attack-vs-normal attention differences, claiming 'the first in transformer-based IoT IDS literature'; (c) Demystifying Network Foundation Models (NeurIPS 2025) probes NFM hidden representations (not attention); (d) model-agnostic perturbation tools (Traffic-Explainer, BiasSeeker, ShortcutCatcher) sidestep attention entirely; (e) a WCNC 2026 paper explicitly calls traffic attention scores 'unstable ... hard interpretation, posing risks in security-critical scenarios'. This is an open validation gap.

papers.title: Attention is not Explanation
papers.relevance: Foundational negative result: attention weights correlate weakly with gradient-based importance and admit adversarial distributions yielding identical predictions -- the benchmark any 'attention heatmap = explanation' claim in traffic transformers must answer.

papers.title: Attention is not not Explanation
papers.relevance: Rebuttal defining testing protocols (uniform-weights baseline, variance calibration, adversarial training of attention) for when attention can serve as explanation; supplies the exact experimental designs a traffic-transformer validation study would need.

papers.title: Is Attention Interpretable?
papers.relevance: Intervention study (zeroing attended representations) showing attention weights only partially indicate importance -- the third leg of the debate canon relevant to byte-token attention in traffic models.

papers.title: Why Attention is Not Explanation: Surgical Intervention and Causal Reasoning about Neural Models
papers.authors: Christopher Grimsley, Elijah Mayfield, Julia R. S. Bursten
papers.relevance: Argues from causal-inference grounds that attention-as-explanation fails because surgical interventions on attention are not well-defined causal manipulations; sharpens what 'validated as explanation' would even mean.

papers.title: Is Attention Explanation? An Introduction to the Debate
papers.relevance: Survey consolidating the attention-explanation debate across communities; notes 'the lack of communication is becoming more and more tangible' -- traffic/security is precisely such a disconnected community that reuses attention heatmaps uncritically.

papers.title: Quantifying Attention Flow in Transformers
papers.relevance: Attention rollout/flow: raw per-layer attention is unreliable in deep transformers because information mixes across layers; directly undermines single-layer attention heatmaps of the kind shown for 12-layer traffic BERTs.

papers.title: Transformer Interpretability Beyond Attention Visualization
papers.authors: Hila Chefer, Shir Gur, Lior Wolf
papers.relevance: LRP-based relevance propagation through self-attention as a principled alternative to raw attention maps; the natural candidate method for ViT-style traffic models (YaTC's MFR-matrix ViT) that nobody has yet applied to traffic.

papers.title: GNNExplainer: Generating Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
papers.relevance: Canonical post-hoc GNN explainer (mutual-information-maximal subgraph + feature mask); the method most frequently borrowed by GNN-based NIDS/botnet papers to claim explainability.

papers.title: Parameterized Explainer for Graph Neural Network (PGExplainer)
papers.relevance: Amortized, inductive GNN explainer generalizing across instances -- the second standard baseline in security-graph explanation evaluations (malware CFGs, NIDS flow graphs).

papers.title: A Survey of Explainable Graph Neural Networks: Taxonomy and Evaluation Metrics
papers.relevance: Taxonomy and metrics (fidelity, sparsity, stability) for GNN explanations; supplies the evaluation vocabulary missing from most GNN-NIDS explainability papers.

papers.title: Jointly Attacking Graph Neural Network and its Explanations (GEAttack)
papers.relevance: Shows GNNExplainer/PGExplainer explanations can be adversarially manipulated together with predictions -- a robustness caveat that transfers directly to adversarial network-traffic settings.

papers.title: CF-GNNExplainer: Counterfactual Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
papers.relevance: Minimal edge-deletion counterfactuals for GNNs; the template for counterfactual explanation work now appearing in graph-based IDS (e.g. counterfactual GraphLIME defenses).

papers.title: ET-BERT: A Contextualized Datagram Representation with Pre-training Transformers for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.authors: Xinjie Lin, Gang Xiong, Gaopeng Gou, Zhen Li, Junzheng Shi, Jing Yu
papers.relevance: The dominant 12-layer/12-head traffic BERT. Verified from full text: its 'Interpretability' section (4.4) contains only a cipher-randomness analysis (performance attributed to 'the imperfect randomness of the ciphers of encrypted payloads') and t-SNE of representations -- attention weights are never analyzed or validated as explanations.

papers.title: Yet Another Traffic Classifier: A Masked Autoencoder Based Traffic Transformer with Multi-Level Flow Representation (YaTC)
papers.authors: Ruijie Zhao, Mingwei Zhan, Xianwen Deng, Yanhao Wang, Yijun Wang, Guan Gui, Zhi Xue
papers.relevance: MAE-pretrained ViT over an MFR byte matrix with packet-level and flow-level attention modules. Verified from full text: zero interpretability content -- attention is ablated only for accuracy/complexity (ISCXVPN2016, ISCXTor2016, USTC-TFC2016, CICIoT2022); no attention map is ever shown or validated.

papers.title: TrafficFormer: An Efficient Pre-trained Model for Traffic Data
papers.authors: Guangmeng Zhou, Xiongwen Guo, Zhuotao Liu, Tong Li, Qi Li, Ke Xu
papers.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
papers.relevance: State-of-the-art traffic BERT (built on ET-BERT code) adding an SODF pre-training task and field-random-initialization augmentation 'to help the traffic model focus on key information', evaluated on protocol-understanding tasks -- but makes no explainability claim and no attention-faithfulness validation.

papers.title: Self-attentive deep learning method for online traffic classification and its interpretability (SAM)
papers.authors: Guorui Xie, Qing Li, Yong Jiang
papers.relevance: The clearest instance of attention-weights-as-explanation for traffic: treats initial packet bytes as language, reads self-attention weights as per-byte/header-field importance and cross-checks them against protocol semantics -- but performs no faithfulness test of the Jain-Wallace kind.

papers.title: A Feasible and Explainable Network Traffic Classifier Utilizing DistilBERT
papers.relevance: Distilled traffic BERT with an explicit XAI pass that maps learned feature importance back onto packet-structure positions ('analyzed the relationships between the features by associating them with the packet structure') -- one of the few transformer-for-traffic papers with a dedicated explanation analysis.

papers.title: Demystifying Network Foundation Models
papers.relevance: First systematic interpretability audit of traffic foundation models (cites both ET-BERT and YaTC): probes hidden representations via embedding geometry, alignment with domain-expert features, and causal protocol perturbations, finding 'significant anisotropy, inconsistent feature sensitivity patterns, an inability to separate the high-level context, [and] payload dependency' across all four NFMs tested.

papers.title: Building Transparency in Deep Learning-Powered Network Traffic Classification: A Traffic-Explainer Framework
papers.relevance: Model-agnostic input-perturbation explainer (mutual-information-maximizing masks over sequential traffic inputs) for DL traffic models -- explicitly built because operators distrust opaque models; sidesteps attention rather than validating it.

papers.title: ShortcutCatcher: Making Traffic Classification Reliable
papers.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Networking
papers.relevance: Uses explainable-AI attribution to automatically detect and mitigate shortcut learning in traffic classifiers by contrasting model behavior across a training and a differently-collected verification dataset -- XAI as a debugging instrument for exactly the models in this corpus.

papers.title: Bias in the Shadows: Explore Shortcuts in Encrypted Network Traffic Classification (BiasSeeker)
papers.relevance: Semi-automated, model-agnostic shortcut/bias discovery for encrypted-traffic classifiers; motivated by the observation that 'existing solutions heavily rely on model-specific interpretation techniques, which lack adaptability and generality across different model architectures'.

papers.title: Traffic-CBM: A Structurally Interpretable Multimodal Framework for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.relevance: Concept-bottleneck alternative to post-hoc explanation for traffic (cites ET-BERT and YaTC as opaque baselines): organizes flow statistics, packet sequences and byte representations into an explicit concept space because existing fusions yield 'opaque latent features, making it unclear which type of evidence actually drives the prediction'.

papers.title: Multi-Task Scenario Encrypted Traffic Classification and Parameter Analysis (PETReLM)
papers.relevance: LoRA fine-tuning of a BERT traffic model with a transformer-internals analysis: SVD of query-projection matrices across layers shows lower layers filter task-relevant representations while higher layers process abstract features -- weight-level (not attention-level) interpretability of a traffic transformer; future work names 'deeper interpretability'.

papers.title: The Attention-Based Autoencoder for Network Traffic Classification with Interpretable Feature Representation (AMAE)
papers.relevance: Builds attention into an autoencoder expressly so the attention over global spatial structure yields interpretable feature representations of traffic classes -- attention-as-explanation by construction, again without faithfulness testing.

papers.title: Hybrid attention-enhanced explainable model for encrypted traffic detection and classification
papers.relevance: Recent journal paper coupling hybrid attention modules with an explainability component for encrypted traffic detection -- representative of the 2025 wave that treats attention outputs as the explanation artifact.

papers.title: Neurosymbolic Learning for Advanced Persistent Threat Detection under Extreme Class Imbalance
papers.authors: Quhura Fathima, Neda Moghim, et al.
papers.relevance: The only retrieved instance of statistical attention-weight validation on traffic: aggregates per-layer/head [CLS] attention over 14 flow-feature tokens of a BERT (SCVIC-APT-2021) and statistically verifies attack-vs-normal attention differences, claiming 'quantified statistical validation, which is the first in transformer-based IoT IDS literature' -- flow-feature tokens, though, not raw bytes as in ET-BERT/YaTC.

papers.title: XG-BoT: An Explainable Deep Graph Neural Network for Botnet Detection and Forensics
papers.relevance: Applies GNNExplainer plus saliency maps to a grouped-reversible GNN botnet detector to highlight suspicious flows/nodes for forensics -- the archetype of GNNExplainer-borrowed-into-network-security.

papers.title: Evaluating Explainability of Graph Neural Networks for Network Intrusion Detection with Structural Attacks
papers.authors: Dimitri Galli, Andrea Venturi, Isabella Marasco, Mirco Marchetti
papers.relevance: Rare head-to-head evaluation of five XAI techniques on GNN-based NIDS without ground-truth explanations, using explanation-guided structural attacks as the yardstick; finds Integrated Gradients most accurate -- and shows accurate explanations double as attacker reconnaissance.

papers.title: X-CBA: Explainability Aided CatBoosted Anomal-E for Intrusion Detection System
papers.relevance: Couples the self-supervised Anomal-E GNN pipeline with explainability (PFI/SHAP-style local-global analysis) for edge-embedding-based NIDS -- explicit attempt to make GNN NIDS decisions analyst-legible.

papers.title: TE-G-SAGE: Explainable Edge-Aware Graph Neural Networks for Network Intrusion Detection
papers.relevance: Edge-aware GNN NIDS designed for interpretability, motivated by the observation that graph models 'are frequently difficult to interpret, in contrast to many classical approaches' -- provides edge-level explanations on NetFlow benchmark graphs.

papers.title: XG-NID: Dual-Modality Network Intrusion Detection using a Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network and Large Language Model
papers.relevance: Heterogeneous flow+packet graph NIDS whose explanations are rendered as human-readable rationales via an LLM layer -- the emerging GNN-plus-LLM answer to explanation delivery in intrusion detection.

papers.title: On the Consistency of GNN Explanations for Malware Detection
papers.relevance: Evaluates GNNExplainer, PGExplainer and CaptumExplainer for stability/consistency on control-flow-graph malware detection and proposes RankFusion aggregation -- the explanation-quality methodology GNN-NIDS work lacks, in a sibling security domain.

papers.title: Explainable Malware Detection through Integrated Graph Reduction and Learning Techniques
papers.relevance: Combines graph-reduction with GNNExplainer on control/function-call graphs, showing explanation quality survives graph compression -- relevant to scaling GNN explanations to large traffic graphs.

papers.title: E-GraphSAGE: A Graph Neural Network based Intrusion Detection System for IoT
papers.relevance: The edge-feature GraphSAGE NIDS that most GNN-NIDS explainability papers (XG-BoT, TE-G-SAGE, X-CBA, E-GraphSAGE-with-explainability follow-ups) take as the model-under-explanation.

papers.title: Anomal-E: A Self-Supervised Network Intrusion Detection System based on Graph Neural Networks
papers.relevance: Self-supervised edge-embedding GNN NIDS; the base system that X-CBA retrofits with explainability -- included as the second GNN hub for citation expansion.

papers.title: Snort Meets Transformers: Accelerating Transformer-Based Network Traffic Classification for Real-Time Performance
papers.relevance: Extracts SHAP attributions from a transformer traffic model and compiles them into Snort signature rules -- explanation used as knowledge-distillation channel from transformer to rule-based IDS.

papers.title: Explainable Stacking Models based on Complementary Traffic Embeddings
papers.relevance: Stacking meta-learner over complementary traffic embeddings (including transformer embeddings) whose meta-level provides explainability about which embedding type and data source drive each outcome.

papers.title: EBSNN: Extended Byte Segment Neural Network for Network Traffic Classification
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing 19(5)
papers.relevance: Pre-transformer byte-segment RNN with attention over header/payload segments -- the earlier attention-over-bytes lineage whose attention weights were likewise presented as indicating discriminative segments.

papers.title: I2RNN: An Incremental and Interpretable Recurrent Neural Network for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
papers.relevance: Interpretable-by-design RNN with sequential fingerprints and local interpretation of per-segment contributions for encrypted traffic -- the strongest non-transformer 'interpretable architecture' baseline in this sub-literature.

papers.title: DQSA: Dynamic Quantized Self-Attention for Multi-Task Encrypted Network Traffic Classification
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
papers.relevance: Argues different tasks attend to distinct regions of the traffic sequence and proposes dynamic, interpretable attention for multi-task classification -- attention interpretability claimed as a design property, again unvalidated against faithfulness criteria.

papers.title: ExpMD: an Explainable Framework for Traffic Identification Based on Multi-Domain Features
papers.relevance: Explainable traffic-identification framework that splits network information into four feature domains and attributes decisions to domains -- addresses 'underutilization of information and weak interpretability' in traffic DL.

papers.title: LAMBERT: Leveraging Attention Mechanisms to Improve the BERT Fine-Tuning Model for Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.relevance: Adds a cross-granularity attention fine-tuning head over ET-BERT-style pre-training to fuse packet and byte features -- exemplifies attention added for accuracy with interpretability implied but untested.

papers.title: Session Aware Encrypted Traffic Classification with Contextual Position Selection
papers.relevance: One of the only traffic papers to state the attention-explanation problem outright -- prior methods 'rely on attention mechanisms with unstable scores and hard interpretation, posing risks in security-critical scenarios' -- and to design an alternative position-selection mechanism because of it.

papers.title: Exploring the Potential and Boundaries of KAN in Encrypted Traffic Classification
papers.relevance: Replaces MLP blocks with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for 'end-to-end interpretable encrypted traffic classification' via spline-function visualization -- the interpretable-architecture-swap answer to the same opacity complaint ('traditional deep learning-based encrypted traffic classification models generally suffer from weak interpretability').

papers.title: Attention and Representation Learning in Byte-Level Digital Forensics: A Survey of Methods, Challenges, and Applications
papers.venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications 17(2)
papers.relevance: Survey of attention/representation learning over raw bytes (traffic and forensics) that explicitly lists interpretability, dataset bias, distribution shift and reproducibility as open challenges of byte-level attention models.

notes: KEY FINDING (the question asked): attention weights in the flagship traffic transformers have NEVER been validated as explanations. Verified from full PDFs: ET-BERT's 'Interpretability' Sec 4.4 = cipher-randomness analysis ('the effectiveness and generalization of ET-BERT [is] due to the imperfect randomness of the ciphers of encrypted payloads') plus t-SNE -- no attention analysis; YaTC's paper contains no interpretability content at all (16-head packet-level + flow-level attention ablated only for F1/complexity); TrafficFormer (S&P'25) claims no explainability (abstract: field random-initialization augmentation 'helps the traffic model focus on key information'; repo based on ET-BERT code, no attention analysis). The Jain-Wallace / Wiegreffe-Pinter / Serrano-Smith debate and its tooling (adversarial attention, rollout, LRP-relevance) has essentially not been imported into traffic ML. Closest existing evidence: SAM (Computer Networks 2021) reads attention as byte/header importance and sanity-checks against protocol semantics; a 2026 neurosymbolic APT paper (arXiv 2603.00453) aggregates [CLS] attention over 14 flow-feature tokens and runs statistical attack-vs-normal validation, itself claiming to be 'the first in transformer-based IoT IDS literature'; WCNC'26 session-aware paper attacks attention head-on: 'attention mechanisms with unstable scores and hard interpretation, posing risks in security-critical scenarios'. RECURRING DATASETS: ISCXVPN2016 and ISCXTor2016 (nearly universal), USTC-TFC2016, CICIoT2022/CICIoT2023, CSTNET-TLS 1.3 (ET-BERT), CIC-IDS2017/2018, NF-series NetFlow graphs (NF-ToN-IoT, NF-BoT-IoT, NF-UNSW-NB15 -- standard for GNN NIDS), CTU-13 (botnet), SCVIC-APT-2021, CESNET-QUIC22 (newer). RECURRING MODELS: ET-BERT, YaTC, TrafficFormer, NetGPT/Lens/netFound/NetMamba (foundation-model wave; four NFMs audited in Demystifying), ViT/MAE variants, E-GraphSAGE and Anomal-E (GNN NIDS hubs), GCN/GAT/GraphSAGE. RECURRING EXPLANATION METHODS: raw attention visualization (SAM, AMAE, LAMBERT, DQSA -- always qualitative); SHAP/IG/Captum ported onto transformers and GNNs (Snort-meets-Transformers, ITASEC eval, XGNN-IDS-style Captum studies); GNNExplainer/PGExplainer ports (XG-BoT, malware CFG work); model-agnostic perturbation (Traffic-Explainer, BiasSeeker, ShortcutCatcher); representation probing (Demystifying's geometry/alignment/causal-sensitivity, PETReLM's SVD of projection matrices); interpretable-by-design swaps (Traffic-CBM concept bottleneck, KAN, I2RNN). AUTHOR-STATED LIMITATIONS seen: Demystifying-NFM: all four NFMs show 'significant anisotropy, inconsistent feature sensitivity patterns, an inability to separate the high-level context, payload dependency'; Traffic-CBM on prior work: fused features are 'opaque latent features, making it unclear which type of evidence actually drives the prediction'; BiasSeeker: model-specific interpretation techniques 'lack adaptability and generality across different model architectures and deployment scenarios'; PETReLM: 'packet-level identification introduces inherent limitations' (DoS vs DDoS payload similarity), future work = 'deeper interpretability'; ITASEC eval: no ground-truth explanations exist for NIDS graphs, IG most accurate, and good explanations empower attackers (dual-use); TE-G-SAGE: GNN NIDS models 'frequently difficult to interpret, in contrast to many classical approaches'; Bibal (debate survey): 'the lack of communication is becoming more and more tangible' across communities; ET-BERT implicitly concedes dependence on imperfect cipher randomness (a validity threat for its learned features under stronger encryption). GAP THE CORPUS EXPOSES: GNN-side security work borrows explainers wholesale but almost never evaluates explanation quality (only ITASEC'25 and the malware-consistency paper do); transformer-side traffic work either shows unvalidated attention heatmaps or abandons attention for model-agnostic/by-design methods; nobody has run deletion/sufficiency, adversarial-attention, or rollout-style faithfulness tests on ET-BERT/YaTC/TrafficFormer -- a directly actionable research opening.
